claims.text: Conventional PGM nanoscale catalysts produced by standard procedures have approximately 5 nm particles with minimal lattice strain.
Reducing PGM particle size from approximately 5 nm to approximately 3 nm induces appreciable lattice strain.
The proposed particle-size reduction can be achieved without changing catalyst composition.
Nanoparticle lattice strain alters the electronic structure of PGM surface active sites.
Nanoparticle lattice strain alters the geometry of PGM surface active sites.
Strain-induced electronic changes modulate the adsorption energy of ethanol on PGM active sites.
Strain-induced electronic changes modulate the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The strain-induced adsorption changes facilitate removal of surface-poisoning species.
Facilitated removal of poisoning species promotes more efficient ethanol-oxidation pathways.
Lattice strain stabilizes the catalyst structure during repeated potential cycling.
Smaller, more highly strained particles will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than the approximately 5 nm baseline.
Smaller, more highly strained particles will shift product selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products.
Smaller, more highly strained particles will retain activity better during extended cycling than the approximately 5 nm baseline.
The proposed strain mechanism is expected to apply to ethanol oxidation in acidic electrolyte near 70 degrees Celsius under cyclic-voltammetry operation.
